confirmedFindings.quote: TPO runs $7–$12/sq ft over separate polyiso, per commercial cost guides
confirmedFindings.issue: No fact pack contains a $7–$12/sq ft TPO installed-cost range. Every sourced TPO installed cost is the flat NJ figure $8–$12/sq ft (Josten Roofing), appearing at facts-materials-economics.md line 289 (§0 NJ table) and line 363 (§6 'NJ install $/sqft (TPO proxy) | TPO flat $8–$12/sqft | Josten Roofing'). PVC is $6–$12 (line 360); SPF is $4–$8 (line 370). The author's own GAP note (draft spray-foam-vs-tpo.md line 96) concedes the $7–$12 figure is merely 'consistent with commercial cost guides,' i.e. not actually present in a pack — so pinning '$7–$12 ... per commercial cost guides' over-attributes to a source the packs do not show stating it (R10 'use only figures present in the research files'; R9 in-text attribution must name an authority that supports the claim). The defect recurs in directAnswer, comparisonRows[0].itemB, content[0], and content[2]. content[0] is internally self-contradicting: it prints '$7–$12 (NJ TPO flat $8–$12 per Josten Roofing)', citing the sourced $8–$12 in the same breath as the unsourced $7–$12.
confirmedFindings.fix: Replace the unsourced $7–$12 TPO range with the pack-sourced $8–$12 (Josten Roofing) everywhere. directAnswer: 'while TPO runs $7–$12/sq ft over separate polyiso, per commercial cost guides' → 'while TPO runs $8–$12/sq ft over separate polyiso, per Josten Roofing (NJ).' comparisonRows[0].itemB: '$7–$12' → '$8–$12'. detailedAnalysis[0].content[0]: 'SPF runs $4–$8 per square foot and TPO $7–$12 (NJ TPO flat $8–$12 per Josten Roofing), per commercial cost guides and Josten Roofing' → 'SPF runs $4–$8 per square foot and TPO $8–$12, per commercial cost guides and Josten Roofing (NJ)' (drop the now-redundant parenthetical). detailedAnalysis[0].content[2]: 'TPO runs $7–$12 per square foot, $8–$12 in NJ per Josten Roofing' → 'TPO runs $8–$12 per square foot in NJ per Josten Roofing'. SPF $4–$8 (commercial cost guides, line 370) is sourced and stays.
confirmedFindings.refuteReason: Verified directly against facts-materials-economics.md: a full grep of all research packs for '$7' / '7–12' returned ZERO hits (saved tool output), while the SPF $4–$8 (line 370) and TPO flat $8–$12 (lines 289, 363) ARE present. confirmedFindings.quote: Spray polyurethane foam installs only in dry, low-wind weather above roughly 50°F, narrowing the NJ application window, while TPO welds year-round
confirmedFindings.issue: The 'dry, low-wind, above ~50°F' SPF application-window figure appears in no fact pack. The §6 SPF 'Key facts / failure modes' row (facts-materials-economics.md line 372) lists ONLY: foam is UV-sensitive and must stay coated; seamless/monolithic + adds insulation; failures = blistering (trapped moisture/poor prep), adhesion loss, coating erosion under ponding; NRCA requires positive drainage. It states no temperature, wind, or 'dry' install condition. The only 'dry surface / wind under ~15 mph' in any pack is for infrared moisture surveys (facts-materials-economics.md §7 line 389, ASTM C1153) — an unrelated context. The specific '~50°F / low-wind / dry' numbers are fabricated, and njSpecific.content[2] over-attributes them to 'NRCA guidance.' This drives the 'Install Conditions' comparisonRow (itemA 'Dry, low-wind, above ~50°F'), its B winner, and the TPO-wins-on-year-round-install claim in the verdict.
confirmedFindings.fix: Drop the unsourced numeric weather window; keep only the pack-supported qualitative contrast. njSpecific.content[2]: 'Spray polyurethane foam installs only in dry, low-wind weather above roughly 50°F, narrowing the NJ application window, while TPO welds year-round, a scheduling difference under Newark's 35–45 winter freeze-thaw cycles, per NRCA guidance and NOAA normals.' → 'Spray polyurethane foam is a weather-sensitive field-spray application, narrowing its NJ installation window relative to heat-welded TPO, which installs year-round, a scheduling difference across a north-NJ winter (regional estimate of roughly 35–45 freeze-thaw cycles).' (This fold also resolves F4.) comparisonRows[8] 'Install Conditions' itemA: 'Dry, low-wind, above ~50°F' → 'Weather-sensitive field spray' (or remove the row, since no figure defends it). commercialSection.content[2]: change 'SPF's weather-limited spray extends' to retain only the qualitative 'weather-sensitive field spray' framing (already qualitative there; no numeric change needed). If a real SPF spray-temperature/wind spec is wanted, source it to a named SPFA/manufacturer application bulletin in a pack first.
confirmedFindings.refuteReason: Verified directly against facts-materials-economics.md line 372 (the entire SPF fact set) — no install-weather spec exists; a grep of all packs for '50°F / low-wind / dry / application window / weather-sensitive' returned only the unrelated IR-survey line 389 and DOE >50°F-cooler surface fact (line 263). Survives under R10 (zero fabricated figures) and R9 (the 'per NRCA guidance' attribution is unsupported).

confirmedFindings.quote: SPF recovers EPDM, TPO, modified bitumen, or built-up roofing without tear-off, provided the NRCA-required positive drainage is present
confirmedFindings.issue: The 'SPF recovers EPDM, TPO, modified bitumen, or BUR without tear-off' / 'sprays directly over a sound existing membrane after prep, per the SPFA' claim is over-attributed to the SPFA. The §6 SPF pack row (facts-materials-economics.md line 372) states only that SPF is seamless/monolithic, adds insulation, is UV-sensitive, and that the NRCA requires positive drainage — it says NOTHING about spraying SPF over existing EPDM/TPO/mod-bit/BUR without tear-off. No pack lists SPF as a recover-over-existing system. Every recover/tear-off provision in the packs (IRC R908.3.1.1, N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4, ARMA, GAF TAB-R-145 in facts-replacement-reroofing-insurance.md) is about asphalt-shingle recover, not SPF, and none is attributed to the SPFA. The substrate list and no-tear-off claim are pinned to a named source (SPFA) the packs do not show supporting it.
confirmedFindings.fix: Attribute only what the pack supports. faqs[1].answer: 'Spray polyurethane foam applies directly over a sound existing flat roof after surface prep, per the SPFA. SPF recovers EPDM, TPO, modified bitumen, or built-up roofing without tear-off, provided the NRCA-required positive drainage is present.' → 'Spray polyurethane foam is a seamless, monolithic field-sprayed system that adds insulation, and the NRCA requires positive drainage beneath it, per the SPFA and NRCA.' commercialSection.content[0]: 'SPF sprays directly over a sound existing membrane after prep, adding R-6.0–6.5 per inch without tear-off, per the SPFA, where positive drainage exists' → 'SPF is a seamless monolithic spray that adds R-6.0–6.5 per inch of insulation, per ICC-ES and the SPFA, where the NRCA-required positive drainage exists.' Drop the unsourced 'recovers EPDM/TPO/mod-bit/BUR without tear-off' unless a pack adds a named SPFA/manufacturer recover-over source.
confirmedFindings.refuteReason: Verified directly against facts-materials-economics.md line 372 (full SPF fact set — no recover/tear-off claim) and a grep of all packs for 'recover / tear-off / over existing' (saved tool output): every recover-over provision is asphalt-shingle/ARMA/GAF/IRC R908 in facts-replacement-reroofing-insurance.md, none attributed to SPFA, none about SPF. Survives under R9 (attribute only what the named source states) and R10.

confirmedFindings.quote: Newark's 35–45 winter freeze-thaw cycles, per NRCA guidance and NOAA normals
confirmedFindings.issue: The 35–45 freeze-thaw count is over-attributed to 'NOAA normals.' facts-nj-regulatory-climate.md line 141 sources the figure to 'Industry/regional estimates' and line 142 explicitly flags it: 'Source: regional roofing guidance. [UNVERIFIED — not a NOAA-published metric; treat the 35–45 figure as an estimate, not an official statistic.]' The gold exemplar (asphalt-shingles-vs-metal, material-vs-material.ts line 44) handles this correctly — it pins only the 31.5-in snowfall to NOAA 1991–2020 normals and presents 'roughly 35–45 freeze-thaw cycles' with no NOAA attribution; the modified-bitumen-vs-BUR sibling (lines 1048–1049) likewise attributes 35–45 to 'regional climate estimates,' reserving NOAA for the snowfall/temperature normals. This object alone pins the explicitly-NOT-NOAA, [UNVERIFIED]-flagged estimate to NOAA.
confirmedFindings.fix: Strip the NOAA attribution from the freeze-thaw count. 'a scheduling difference under Newark's 35–45 winter freeze-thaw cycles, per NRCA guidance and NOAA normals.' → 'a scheduling difference across the roughly 35–45 freeze-thaw cycles a typical north-NJ winter sees (regional estimate).' NOTE: this fix folds into F2 — if F2's qualitative rewrite of njSpecific.content[2] is applied (which already drops the NOAA attribution and frames 35–45 as a regional estimate), F4 is resolved in the same edit; do not double-apply.
confirmedFindings.refuteReason: Verified directly against facts-nj-regulatory-climate.md line 142, which carries an explicit '[UNVERIFIED — not a NOAA-published metric]' flag on the 35–45 figure, and against the committed sibling treatment (material-vs-material.ts lines 44, 1048–1049) that pins 35–45 to regional estimates, never NOAA. Survives under R10 ([UNVERIFIED] figure must not be presented as an official statistic) and R9 (mis-attribution to NOAA).
